deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page, and none of it is by Riemann. Folio 12av is the back of an archivist's note sheet (graph paper) from 1986. The faint writing visible in the image is the ink of the front (12a) showing through in mirror image. The lines are written right-to-left, the letter forms are reversed, and the layout matches the front line for line: the heading 'Zu Riemann 13', a seven-line German paragraph, the reference line, the date and signature, and the small note at the lower left. The content is therefore identical to the previous page. That page records that the fair copy of Riemann's 1851 dissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse' (35 pp., quarto) was sold in 1979 at a Sotheby's auction (Honeyman Collection) to a private buyer for £1,400. Its source is American Book Prices Current 1979, p. 1014, and it is dated 29.10.86 and signed (H. Rohlfing?). There are no formulas, derivations or computations to reconstruct. The note is a 20th-century provenance remark about Cod. Ms. Riemann 13, the dissertation material that begins on the next folio.
errors: The machine transcription treats show-through as independent writing on this side. The verso is effectively blank; the visible text is the mirror image of 12a.

Because the text was read in mirror image, the transcription introduces readings that conflict with the front: '31 S.' should be '35 S.', '£ 11000' should be '£ 1.400', and the date '25.11.86' should be '29.10.86'. The signature '?. Rosen' is a misreading of the signature on the front (H. Rohlfing?).
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a blank verso showing bleed-through of a 1986 archival note about the auction provenance of Riemann's dissertation fair copy. It contains no mathematics and nothing by Riemann.
transcription_corrections: Folio 12av is blank; all visible writing is reversed show-through from folio 12a and should not be transcribed as content of this page.
Where the transcription reads '(= 31 S. 4° (1851))', the front has '35 S. 4° (1851)'.
Where the transcription reads '£ 11000[?]', the front has '£ 1.400'.
Where the transcription reads '25.11.86[?] ?. Rosen[?]', the front has '29.10.86, H. Rohlfing[?]'.
The unread lower-left lines are the mirrored note 'V 11 - Paris / 1979, 1986' from the front.
The 'c.[?]' before the reference is 's.' (siehe) on the front.
